title: Infinity Yoneda evaluation for arbitrary space-valued presheaves
statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small and all categories under discussion fit in $\mathcal U'$. Use the infinity-category, coherent functor and mapping-space conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Small means $\mathcal U$-small, and $\mathcal S$ denotes the infinity category of small spaces. Let $D$ be a small infinity category, let $\mathcal P(D)=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$, and let $j:D\to\mathcal P(D)$ send $d$ to $\operatorname{Map}_D(-,d)$. For every $F\in\mathcal P(D)$ and $d\in D$, evaluation of a coherent transformation at $\operatorname{id}_d$ induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(D)}(j(d),F)\simeq F(d).$$
These equivalences assemble into a natural equivalence of functors on $D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal P(D)$, with all higher homotopies retained.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.2 and the correctly oriented Yoneda-evaluation assertion needed in Lemma 5.5.2.1, printed pp. 324-325 and 462-463. The printed corepresented formulation of Lemma 5.5.2.1 has a variance error; the formula here is the representable-presheaf evaluation formula. Also Kerodon Subsection 8.3.1 (Tag 03M2), Proposition 8.3.1.3 and Remark 8.3.1.5, applied to the opposite category Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks Project tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text:
Put $K_d=D_{/d}$, with projection $r_d:K_d\to D$, and let $e_d$ be its vertex $\operatorname{id}_d$. By [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], $r_d$ is a right fibration, its fiber at $x$ is the right-pinched space $\operatorname{Map}_D(x,d)$, and $K_d$ is small. The right-fibration clause and representable compatibility of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] identify $r_d$ with the presheaf $j(d)$, taking $e_d$ to the identity element. Choose a small right-fibration representative $q_F:E_F\to D$ for $F$. The same node gives equivalences of Kan spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(D)}(j(d),F)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{/D}(K_d,E_F),\qquad (E_F)_d\simeq F(d).$$
Here an $n$-simplex of the middle space is a map $K_d\times\Delta^n\to E_F$ over $D$, with all simplicial parameters retained. The comparison is coherent in its two presheaves and respects restriction and identities.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.2, printed pp.324-325, right-fibration version of the proof; the already cited classification supplies the coherent model comparison.

proof.text:
We prove the particular right-anodyne inclusion $i_d:\{e_d\}\hookrightarrow K_d$ explicitly, rather than assuming a general final-object theorem. An $n$-simplex $\sigma$ of $K_d$ is an $(n+1)$-simplex of $D$ with last vertex $d$. Set $h_n(\sigma)=s_{n+1}^D\sigma$, and set $h_{-1}(*)=e_d$. The faces and degeneracies of $K_d$ are the corresponding operators of $D$ excluding the last face and last degeneracy. Thus the simplicial identities give
$$d_{n+1}h_n=1,\quad d_i h_n=h_{n-1}d_i\ (0\leq i\leq n),\quad h_n s_i=s_i h_{n-1}\ (0\leq i<n),\quad h_{n+1}h_n=s_{n+1}h_n,$$
where in degree zero the second equation reads $d_0h_0=e_d$. These identities append a repeated final vertex, and are valid even when $D$ is not a quasicategory.

source.place: Join-slice definition in Proposition 4.3.6.1; explicit agent calculation of the terminal extra degeneracy.

proof.text:
Call a nondegenerate $n$-simplex $\sigma$ of $K_d$ basic if it is not $e_d$ and is not $h_{n-1}(\tau)$ for any $(n-1)$-simplex (in degree zero only exclude $e_d$). For basic $\sigma$, $h_n\sigma$ is nondegenerate: if $h_n\sigma=s_i\rho$ with $i<n$, applying $d_{n+1}$ makes $\sigma$ degenerate; if $i=n$, first $\rho=\sigma$ and then applying $d_n$ gives $\sigma=h_{n-1}d_n\sigma$, contrary to basicness. In degree zero the latter argument gives $\sigma=e_d$. Conversely, if a nondegenerate simplex is $h\tau$, then $\tau$ is nondegenerate because $h$ commutes with degeneracies, and $\tau$ is basic because $hh$ is degenerate; its preimage $\tau$ is unique by $d_{n+1}h_n=1$. Thus the nondegenerate simplices other than $e_d$ are partitioned into pairs $(\sigma,h_n\sigma)$ with $\sigma$ basic.
Starting with $\{e_d\}$, attach these pairs in increasing dimension $n$ of $\sigma$. For a basic $n$-simplex use its characteristic map $\Delta^{n+1}\to K_d$ corresponding to $h_n\sigma$, and attach along $\Lambda_{n+1}^{n+1}$. Its missing face is $\sigma$; every other face is $h_{n-1}d_i\sigma$ and is already present, as is every proper face of $\sigma$. Distinct pairs have distinct new nondegenerate simplices. The unique nondegenerate decomposition of [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] therefore identifies each stage, degree by degree, with the pushout of the indicated horns: all other simplices are uniquely their degeneracies. All simplices occur after countably many dimension stages. Each attachment is a right horn ($n+1>0$), so closure under pushouts and transfinite composites in [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne] proves $i_d$ right anodyne. Coproducts of the attachments may equivalently be attached one at a time in any well-order of the small indexing set.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-exponentiation] with $A=\{e_d\}$, $B=K_d$, $S=D$, $E=E_F$, and $q=q_F$. Step 3 verifies its right-anodyne hypothesis; step 1 verifies the right-fibration hypothesis. Pull its displayed trivial Kan fibration back along the map
$$(E_F)_d\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(K_d,D)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(\{e_d\},D)}\operatorname{Fun}(\{e_d\},E_F),\qquad z\longmapsto(r_d,z),$$
where $r_d$ is constant in the simplicial parameter. The resulting map is exactly restriction
$$\rho_{d,F}:\operatorname{Fun}_{/D}(K_d,E_F)\longrightarrow(E_F)_d,\qquad u\longmapsto u(e_d).$$
It is a trivial Kan fibration: a boundary lifting problem for a pullback is the same boundary lifting problem for the original map with its base map fixed, so its filler still lies in the pullback. This also covers the empty boundary in dimension zero, as required by [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration].

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.4, right-fibration assertion, followed by the explicit pullback to maps over D.

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence], the map $\rho_{d,F}$ has a section and a simplicial homotopy inverse. Transport it through the two equivalences of step 1. The pullback compatibility in [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], applied to the vertex inclusion $\{d\}\to D$, identifies restriction of a map over $D$ with its component at $d$; its identity compatibility then identifies the resulting map with
$$\varepsilon_{d,F}:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(D)}(j(d),F)\longrightarrow F(d),\qquad\eta\longmapsto\eta_d(\operatorname{id}_d).$$
This proves that the specified evaluation map, with its entire Kan space of parameters, is an equivalence. It does not merely show a bijection on components. The section supplied by the trivial-fibration lemma is used only to verify that this canonical map is an equivalence; no natural choice of those sections is asserted.

source.place: Tag 08NS, lemma-trivial-kan-homotopy; HTT Lemma 5.1.5.2 identifies the map as evaluation on the distinguished identity.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-enriched-presheaf-rectification] to \(D\).  It supplies a small locally Kan
simplicial category \(A\), an equivalence \(q:N_{\mathrm{hc}}A\simeq D\), the projective
simplicial presheaf model \(\mathsf M\), its bifibrant subcategory \(B\), and an equivalence
\(\Theta:N_{\mathrm{hc}}B\simeq\mathcal P(D)\).  The statement of that lemma includes the
\(\mathcal U'\)-small ambient construction, the \(\mathcal U\)-small values, and compatibility
with mapping complexes, evaluation, composition and identities, together with the coherent
comparisons of the representable diagram and of the two bifunctors on \(A^{\mathrm{op}}\times B\).  Thus
all data needed for the strict enriched model below satisfy the stated universe hypotheses.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1 and Proposition 4.2.4.4, with Appendix A.3.3; the supporting statement is the explicit enriched rectification application.

proof.text:
In the model supplied by [lem-coef-enriched-presheaf-rectification], apply
[lem-coef-enriched-yoneda-evaluation].  For \(Y_a=A(-,a)\), it gives the strict enriched
transformation
\[
\widetilde\varepsilon_{a,P}:\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathsf M}(Y_a,P)\to P(a),
\qquad \alpha\mapsto\alpha_a(1_a),
\]
together with its action-defined inverse.  Its statement verifies the full simplicial
naturality in \(a\) and \(P\), including composition and units, so this is one enriched
natural transformation on \(A^{\mathrm{op}}\times B\), not merely a family of edge maps.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1 and Appendix A.3.3; strict enriched Yoneda calculation supplied by the supporting lemma.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-enriched-nerve-transformation] to the two enriched functors and the
transformation of step 7.  Its interval construction gives a simplicial functor
\(A^{\mathrm{op}}\times B\times[1]\to\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal U}\), hence a coherent
transformation after taking \(N_{\mathrm{hc}}\).  By its restriction and whiskering clauses and the coherent bifunctor and representable comparisons of [lem-coef-enriched-presheaf-rectification], the endpoints identify through \(\Theta\) and \(q\) with the mapping and evaluation
functors in the item, and the component is still evaluation at \(1_a\).  Therefore every
higher simplex and the identity comparison are retained when the transformation is
transported to \(D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal P(D)\).

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1 and Proposition 4.2.4.4; coherent-nerve interval construction in the supporting statement.

proof.text: Apply the pointwise equivalence criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] to the actual transformation $\varepsilon$ of step 8. Use that statement with $\mathcal U'$ as its smallness universe: $D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal P(D)$ is $\mathcal U'$-small, as are the model $B$ and the category $\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$ used above, since $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$. Thus its hypothesis that the parameter simplicial set be small is satisfied. Every component of $\varepsilon$ is the equivalence of step 5, so $\varepsilon$ is an equivalence in the functor category. The values $F(d)$ and the mapping spaces in the assertion remain $\mathcal U$-small. No nonempty-value assumption was made. If $F(d)$ is empty then the map in step 4 has both source and target empty; if $D$ is empty the parameter category is empty and its unique transformation is an equivalence.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1 and Proposition 4.2.4.4 (printed pp.89 and 258), with the projective simplicial diagram model of Appendix A.3.3. The coherence argument here is the explicit enriched evaluation construction, not the free-cocompletion universal property.
